hmmt-feb-2008-alg-02.title: Find the intervals for each value of f

hmmt-feb-2008-alg-03.title: Use the parabola
hmmt-feb-2008-alg-03.body:
Let $f(x)=x^2+2ax+3a$, an upward parabola. $|f(x)|\le2$ has exactly one solution only if the parabola touches the strip $-2\le y\le 2$ at a single point, i.e. its minimum value is exactly $2$; if the minimum were below $2$, the parabola would meet the strip on a whole interval (or the minimum is $<-2$ and it crosses it twice).

The minimum is $f(-a)=3a-a^2$. Setting $3a-a^2=2$ gives $a^2-3a+2=0$, so $a=1$ or $a=2$. Check $a=1$: $(x+1)^2+2\le2$ only at $x=-1$. For $a=2$: $(x+2)^2+2\le 2$ only at $x=-2$.

**Answer: $a=1$ or $a=2$**

hmmt-feb-2008-alg-04.title: Pick x and y so two terms cancel
hmmt-feb-2008-alg-04.body:
Put $x=10$, $y=5$: then $2x+y=25=3x-y$, so $f(10)+f(25)+250=f(25)+200+1$, giving $f(10)=-49$.

(Remark: $y=x/2$ gives $f(x)=1-\frac{x^2}{2}$ in general, which satisfies the equation.)

**Answer: $-49$**

hmmt-feb-2008-alg-06.title: Restrict a and b
hmmt-feb-2008-alg-06.body:
The real roots of unity are $\pm1$. A non-real root of unity $\zeta$ of a real quadratic has conjugate $\bar\zeta$ as the other root, so $b=\zeta\bar\zeta=1$ and $|a|=|\zeta+\bar\zeta|\le2$.

So check $z^2+az+1$ for $a\in\{-2,\dots,2\}$: these give $z=\pm1$ ($a=\pm2$), $z=\pm i$ ($a=0$), and $z=\frac12(\pm1\pm\sqrt3 i)$ ($a=\pm1$), all roots of unity. Total: $2+2+4=8$.

**Answer: 8**

hmmt-feb-2008-alg-07.title: Swap the order of summation
hmmt-feb-2008-alg-07.body:
For fixed $k$, $n$ runs from $k+1$ to $\infty$: $\sum_{n>k}2^{-n}=2^{-k}$. So the sum is $\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{k}{2^k}\cdot2^{-k}=\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{k}{4^k}$.

With $\sum_{k\ge1}kx^k=\frac{x}{(1-x)^2}$ at $x=\frac14$: $\frac{1/4}{9/16}=\frac49$.

**Answer: $\frac49$**

hmmt-feb-2008-alg-08.title: Use t = tan 20
hmmt-feb-2008-alg-08.body:
Let $t=\tan20^\circ$. Then $\tan65^\circ=\frac{1+t}{1-t}$ and $2\tan40^\circ=\frac{4t}{1-t^2}$, so the difference is $\frac{(1+t)^2-4t}{1-t^2}=\frac{(1-t)^2}{(1-t)(1+t)}=\frac{1-t}{1+t}=\tan(45^\circ-20^\circ)=\tan25^\circ$.

**Answer: $25^\circ$**

hmmt-feb-2008-alg-09.title: Reduce with y = x + 1/x
hmmt-feb-2008-alg-09.body:
Dividing by $x^2$: $\left(x+\frac1x\right)^2+a\left(x+\frac1x\right)-b-2=0$. With $y=x+\frac1x$, which takes exactly the real values $|y|\ge2$, we need $y^2+ay-(b+2)=0$ to have a root with $|y|\ge2$.

Its discriminant $a^2+4(b+2)>0$, and the root of larger magnitude is the negative one, with absolute value $\frac{a+\sqrt{a^2+4b+8}}{2}$. We need this $\ge2$, i.e. $\sqrt{a^2+4b+8}\ge4-a$. Squaring (both sides nonnegative) gives $4b+8\ge16-8a$, i.e. $b\ge2-2a$.

In the unit square this is the triangle with vertices $(1,0),(1,1),(\tfrac12,1)$, of area $\frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot1=\frac14$.

**Answer: $\frac14$**

hmmt-feb-2008-alg-10.title: Use the generating function of central binomial coefficients
hmmt-feb-2008-alg-10.body:
Since $\binom{2n}{n}=(-4)^n\binom{-1/2}{n}$, the binomial theorem gives $\sum_{n\ge0}\binom{2n}{n}x^n=(1-4x)^{-1/2}$ for $|x|<\frac14$. At $x=\frac15$: $(1-\frac45)^{-1/2}=\sqrt5$.

**Answer: $\sqrt5$**
